    "articleBody": "The Odisha Congress has called for a statewide bandh tomorrow, October 8, raising a series of demands including resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, withdrawal of the MMDR Bill, and the resignation of the state School and Mass Education Minister over alleged errors in textbooks. Advertisment Several non-BJP parties, including CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML), NCP, Forward Bloc, Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, are likely to extend support to the bandh. Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Bhakta Charan Das had announced the bandh in Bhubaneswar on September 29. Advertisment Transport Services, Shops, Markets May Take a Hit The bandh could affect normal life across the state, particularly transport and commercial activities. The Congress has called for suspension of truck, bus, autorickshaw and other vehicular movement during the bandh. Train services may also face disruption as protesters take to the streets. The shutdown could also affect the functioning of government and private offices. Shops, markets and commercial establishments may remain closed during the bandh. Petrol pumps and other business establishments could also face disruption. Meanwhile, the Congress has urged the general public to support the bandh and participate in the protest over the issues raised by the party. With several political parties are likely to extend support, the bandh may have a significant impact on routine activities in different parts of Odisha. “Tomorrow, October 8, railway, bus and other transport services will remain closed as part of the bandh. Only medical stores and hospitals will remain open for the public. Students of Classes 8 and 9 who are scheduled to appear for examinations tomorrow will not be affected by the bandh, allowing them to take their exams peacefully. We have pledged to the people that the bandh will be conducted in a non-violent and peaceful manner, and we have taken this decision to ensure its success,” said Congress leader Santosh Singh Saluja. Emergency Services Exempted The Congress, however, has kept essential and emergency services outside the ambit of the bandh. “We appeal to the citizens who love Odisha, believe in the Constitution and want to protect the republic to come forward and support the bandh. If the BJD or any other political party comes forward to support this cause, we will welcome them, because this is a fight for the interests of Odisha. On behalf of the INDIA Bloc, we appeal to everyone to ensure that the bandh is conducted peacefully. We are fighting for four key interests, and this struggle will continue until we achieve our objective. We are doing this to protect the interests of Odisha,” said Prashant Mishra, State Secretary, CPI(M). Hospitals, ambulance services, fire services and medicine shops will continue to operate. Other essential and emergency services will also remain functional during the shutdown.",

                            "><div id="post-container"><p>The <a href="https://odishatv.in/tags/odisha" target="_blank">Odisha </a>Congress has called for a statewide bandh tomorrow, October 8, raising a series of demands including resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, withdrawal of the MMDR Bill, and the resignation of the state School and Mass Education Minister over alleged errors in textbooks.</p><div class="responsive-ad-css"><div class="publive-dynamic-container  over-hidden article-mid-ads-style bottom-margin" style="margin-top:10px;margin-bottom:10px;width:300px;height:250px;"><span class="publive-slot-span">Advertisment</span><!-- /370089190/Otv_English-Middle_Story_Section-Desktop-Article-300x250-PL-2025 --><div id="div-gpt-ad-1757066960690-0" style="min-width: 300px; min-height: 250px;"><script>
      googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1757066960690-0'); });
    </script><div id="google_ads_iframe_/370089190/Otv_English-Middle_Story_Section-Desktop-Article-300x250-PL-2025_0__container__" style="border: 0pt; margin: auto; text-align: center; width: 300px; height: 0px;"></div></div></div></div><p>Several non-BJP parties, including CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML), NCP, Forward Bloc, Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, are likely to extend support to the bandh.</p><p>Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Bhakta Charan Das had announced the bandh in Bhubaneswar on September 29. </p><div class="responsive-ad-css"><div class="publive-dynamic-container  over-hidden article-mid-ads-style bottom-margin" style="margin-top:10px;margin-bottom:10px;width:300px;height:250px;"><span class="publive-slot-span">Advertisment</span><!-- /370089190/Otv_English-Middle_Story_Section_1-Desktop-Article-300x250-PL-2025 --><div id="div-gpt-ad-1757067001263-0" style="min-width: 300px; min-height: 250px;"><script>
    googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1757067001263-0'); });
  </script></div></div></div><h2><strong>Transport Services, Shops, Markets May Take a Hit</strong></h2><p>The bandh could affect normal life across the state, particularly transport and commercial activities.</p><p>The Congress has called for suspension of truck, bus, autorickshaw and other vehicular movement during the bandh. Train services may also face disruption as protesters take to the streets.</p><p>The shutdown could also affect the functioning of government and private offices.</p><p>Shops, markets and commercial establishments may remain closed during the bandh. Petrol pumps and other business establishments could also face disruption.</p><p>Meanwhile, the Congress has urged the general public to support the bandh and participate in the protest over the issues raised by the party.</p><p>With several political parties are likely to extend support, the bandh may have a significant impact on routine activities in different parts of Odisha.</p><p class="MsoNormal">“Tomorrow, October 8, railway, bus and other transport services will remain closed as part of the bandh. Only medical stores and hospitals will remain open for the public. Students of Classes 8 and 9 who are scheduled to appear for examinations tomorrow will not be affected by the bandh, allowing them to take their exams peacefully. We have pledged to the people that the bandh will be conducted in a non-violent and peaceful manner, and we have taken this decision to ensure its success,” said Congress leader Santosh Singh Saluja.</p><h2><strong>Emergency Services Exempted</strong></h2><p>The Congress, however, has kept essential and emergency services outside the ambit of the bandh.</p><p><o:p> </o:p>“We appeal to the citizens who love Odisha, believe in the Constitution and want to protect the republic to come forward and support the bandh. If the BJD or any other political party comes forward to support this cause, we will welcome them, because this is a fight for the interests of Odisha. On behalf of the INDIA Bloc, we appeal to everyone to ensure that the bandh is conducted peacefully. We are fighting for four key interests, and this struggle will continue until we achieve our objective. We are doing this to protect the interests of Odisha,” said Prashant Mishra, State Secretary, CPI(M).</p><p>Hospitals, ambulance services, fire services and medicine shops will continue to operate. Other essential and emergency services will also remain functional during the shutdown.</p></div></div><div class="tags-category hide_article_content" id="article_tag_11962125"><a href="https://odishatv.in/tags/odisha" class="" aria-label="Odisha" target="_blank">

                    ଦୋକାନବଜାର ବନ୍ଦ, ଗାଡ଼ି ଚଳାଚଳ ଠପ୍‌: କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡାରେ ଓଡ଼ିଶା ବନ୍ଦର ପ୍ରଭାବ                    <br>

                <div class="p-t-20" style="font-size: 18px">
                    <p></p><p>କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡା, ୮।୧୦(ପ୍ରଦୀପ କୁମାର ସାହୁ): ଗୁରୁବାର ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ଓଡ଼ିଶା ବନ୍ଦ ଡାକରାକୁ କଳାହାଣ୍ଡି ଜିଲ୍ଲାର କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡା ବ୍ଲକରେ ସ୍ବତଃସ୍ଫୂର୍ତ୍ତ ସମର୍ଥନ ମିଳିଛି। ବନ୍ଦ ଯୋଗୁ ସକାଳୁ ବ୍ଲକର ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଅଞ୍ଚଳରେ ଦୋକାନବଜାର ବନ୍ଦ ରହିବା ସହ ଗାଡ଼ି ଚଳାଚଳ ଠପ୍‌ ହୋଇପଡ଼ିଛି। ଫଳରେ ରାସ୍ତାଘାଟ ଶୂନଶାନ ହୋଇପଡ଼ିଛି। କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡା ବ୍ଲକ ସଦର ସମେତ ରିଷିଡ଼ା ଓ ଜୋରାଡବରା ଛକ ଆଦି ଅଞ୍ଚଳରେ ବନ୍ଦର ବ୍ୟାପକ ପ୍ରଭାବ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ମିଳିଛି। ବନ୍ଦ ପାଳନକାରୀମାନେ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ସ୍ଥାନରେ ବୁଲି ପିକେଟିଂ କରି ଦୋକାନବଜାର ଓ ଯାନବାହନ ଚଳାଚଳ ବନ୍ଦ କରିଥିଲେ। ବ୍ଲକର ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଶିକ୍ଷାନୁଷ୍ଠାନ ମଧ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ ରହିଥିଲା।</p>
<p>ବନ୍ଦ ଡାକରାରେ ଏମଏମ୍‌ଡିଆର୍‌ ବିଲ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟାହାର, ମୁଖ୍ୟ ନିର୍ବାଚନ କମିଶନର ଜ୍ଞାନେଶ କୁମାରଙ୍କ ଇସ୍ତଫା ଏବଂ ଗଣଶିକ୍ଷା ମନ୍ତ୍ରୀଙ୍କ ଇସ୍ତଫା ଭଳି ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଦାବି ଉଠାଯାଇଛି। ବ୍ଲକ କଂଗ୍ରେସ ସଭାପତି ସୁରେଶ ଚୌଧୁରୀଙ୍କ ନେତୃତ୍ୱରେ କଂଗ୍ରେସ କର୍ମୀମାନେ ବନ୍ଦ ପାଳନରେ ସାମିଲ ହୋଇଥିଲେ। କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡାରେ ଦୀନବନ୍ଧୁ ସାହୁ, ରସ୍ମିକାନ୍ତ ସାହୁ, ରମେଶ ସାହୁ, ହିରୋଜ ସାହୁ, ଆମ୍ବିଲାଳ ସାହୁ, ବିପିନ ସାହୁ ପ୍ରମୁଖ ବନ୍ଦ ପାଳନରେ ଉପସ୍ଥିତ ଥିଲେ। ରିଷିଡ଼ାରେ କଂଗ୍ରେସ ନେତା ଗୋବର୍ଦ୍ଧନ କୁମାର ଓ ମାର୍କଣ୍ଡ ସାହୁଙ୍କ ସହ ସିପିଏମ ନେତା ଶତ୍ରୁଘ୍ନ ରଣାଙ୍କ ନେତୃତ୍ୱରେ କର୍ମୀମାନେ ପିକେଟିଂ କରିଥିଲେ।</p>
<p>ସେହିପରି ଜୋରାଡବରା ଛକରେ କଂଗ୍ରେସ ଜିଲା ଉପସଭାପତି ରାଜକିଶୋର ମିଶ୍ର ଓ ବ୍ଲକ କଂଗ୍ରେସ ସଭାପତି ସୁରେଶ ଚୌଧୁରୀଙ୍କ ନେତୃତ୍ୱରେ ପିକେଟିଂ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା। ଏଥିରେ ନୀଳାମ୍ବର ବେହେରା, ହେମସାଗର ସାହୁ, ଚୈତନ୍ୟ ସାହୁ, ମୁରଲୀ ସାହୁ, ଉମେଶ ସାହୁ, ଲାଭି ରଣା, ଖଗେଶ୍ୱର ସେନାପତି, ଚୈତନ୍ୟ ମାଝୀ, ପୁରୁନ ମାଝୀ, ଡୋଲାମଣି ମାଝୀ, ନାଗୁ ସାହୁ, ରମେଶ ପୁଟେଲଙ୍କ ସମେତ ବହୁ ଦଳୀୟ ନେତା ଓ କର୍ମୀ ସାମିଲ ହୋଇଥିଲେ। ବନ୍ଦ ଯୋଗୁ କର୍ଲାମୁଣ୍ଡା ବ୍ଲକରେ ସାଧାରଣ ଜନଜୀବନ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ ହୋଇଥିବା ବେଳେ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ରାସ୍ତାରେ ଯାନବାହନ ଚଳାଚଳ ନ ଥିବାରୁ ପରିବେଶ ଶୂନଶାନ ଦେଖାଯାଇଥିଲା।</p>
<p> </p>

/*crousel*/
#dw-speaker{
	overflow:hidden;
}
#dw-speaker .item {     
    margin: 0 10px 0 0;
    padding: 0;
    float: left; 
	text-align:center;
	cursor: pointer;
}
#dw-speaker .item h3 {
    font-size: 18px !important;
    line-height: 22px !important;
    margin-bottom: 5px;
    font-weight: 600;
    margin-top: 0;
}
#dw-speaker .item  p{
	font-size:15px;
	line-height:20px;
	margin-bottom:0;
}
#dw-speaker .item:hover {
    transform: scale(1.1);
    transition-duration: 0.25s;
}
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(5):first-child, 
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(5):first-child ~ div.item{
width: calc((100% - 50px) / 5);
}
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(6):first-child, 
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(6):first-child ~ div.item{
width: calc((100% - 60px) / 6);
}
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(7):first-child, 
#dw-speaker .item:nth-last-child(7):first-child ~ div.item{
width: calc((100% - 70px) / 7);
}

.social-toolbar {

            /* Mobile: Follow Us sits on the left, Comment & Share pushed to the right */
            justify-content: space-between;
            gap: 1rem;
            margin-bottom: 1rem;
        }

        /* Left Side: Follow Us Group */
        .follow-us-group {
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 0.75rem;
        }

        .follow-label {
            font-size: 0.875rem;
            font-weight: 600;
            color: #374151;
        }

        .follow-icon-link {
            display: inline-flex;
            align-items: center;
            transition: opacity 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease;
        }

        .follow-icon-link:hover {
            opacity: 0.8;
            transform: scale(1.05);
        }

        .google-news-svg {
            width: 1.75rem;  /* 28px */
            height: 1.75rem; /* 28px */
        }

        .whatsapp-follow-icon {
            font-size: 1.5rem; /* 24px */
            color: #25D366;
        }

        /* Vertical Divider (Desktop Only) */
        .toolbar-divider {
            display: none;
            width: 1px;
            height: 1.25rem;
            background-color: #d1d5db;
        }

        /* Right Side on Mobile / Next to Divider on Desktop: Comment & Share Icons */
        .share-comment-group {
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 0.5rem;
            position: relative;
            margin-left: auto; /* Pushes Comment & Share to the right edge on mobile */
        }

        .share-dropdown-container {
            position: relative;
        }

        .toolbar-icon-btn {
            color: #374151;
            border: none;
            padding: 0.5rem;
            border-radius: 9999px;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            font-size: 20px;
            transition: background-color 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease;
        }

        .toolbar-icon-btn.share-trigger {
            margin-right: -0.5rem; /* Optical alignment with right edge on mobile */
        }

        .toolbar-icon-btn:hover,
        .toolbar-icon-btn.is-active {
            color: #000;
            background-color: #f3f4f6;
        }

        /* Share Dropdown Menu */
        .share-dropdown-menu {
            display: none; /* Hidden by default */
            position: absolute;
            right: 0; /* Aligns to right edge so it stays inside mobile screen */
            margin-top: 0.5rem;
            width: 12rem; /* 192px */
            background-color: #fff;
            border: 1px solid #e5e7eb;
            border-radius: 0.5rem;
            box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0 8px 10px -6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);
            padding: 0.5rem 0;
            z-index: 30;
            transform-origin: top right;
            opacity: 0;
            transform: scale(0.95) translateY(-10px);
            transition: opacity 150ms ease-out, transform 150ms ease-out;
        }

        .share-dropdown-menu.is-visible {
            display: block;
        }

        .share-dropdown-menu.dropdown-enter-active {
            opacity: 1;
            transform: scale(1) translateY(0);
        }

        .dropdown-item {

<div id="postexcerpt"><p>Bhubaneswar, Oct 8 (PTI) Normal life was affected in several districts of Odisha on Thursday as supporters of INDIA bloc parties held demonstrations and blocked roads as part of a 12-hour bandh to protest against a new mining law, errors in school textbooks and the alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.</p><div class="code-block code-block-5" style="margin: 8px 0; clear: both;">
<div id="vdo_ai_div"></div><script>(function(v,d,o,ai){ai=d.createElement('script');ai.defer=true;ai.async=true;ai.src=v.location.protocol+o;d.head.appendChild(ai);})(window, document, '//a.vdo.ai/core/theprint/vdo.ai.js');</script></div>
<p>Business establishments, petrol pumps, shops and many educational institutes were seen closed in the morning, while public transport such as buses and autorickshaws remained off the road.<div id="74b3e53b-d5c7-4bcb-955f-27ffce21ecdd" data-section="74b3e53b-d5c7-4bcb-955f-27ffce21ecdd" class="_ap_apex_ad" data-xpath="#postexcerpt > p:eq(1)" data-section-id="" data-ap-network="adpTags" style="display: block; clear: both; text-align: center; margin: 30px auto 10px; width: 336px; height: 280px; overflow: hidden;" data-render-time="1795339835491">

<div class="third-para"><p>The protesters, holding party flags and banners, staged demonstrations in various places and blocked roads and national highways in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Bargarh, Bhadrak, Balasore, Rayagada, Kendrapara, Bolangir, Berhampur, and Sambalpur.</p>

				</span>
				</button></div></div><div id="postcontent"><p>They picketed at major junctions across the state and burnt tyres to enforce the bandh.</p><p>A number of buses, trucks, taxis, and autorickshaws were stopped in several districts.</p><p>Due to the shutdown, commuters faced hardship reaching their destinations. Many people were seen waiting at bus stops because public transport services were disrupted.<div id="10252c79-9590-4ddb-bf89-9e882cc5d4fb" data-section="10252c79-9590-4ddb-bf89-9e882cc5d4fb" class="_ap_apex_ad" data-xpath="#postcontent > p:eq(2)" data-section-id="" data-ap-network="adpTags" style="display: block; clear: both; text-align: center; margin: 10px auto; width: 728px; height: 90px; overflow: hidden;" data-render-time="1795339835483">

		</script>
	</div>
	</div></p><p>However, essential services such as hospitals, ambulances, fire services, medicine shops and milk supply were exempted from the bandh, a Congress leader said.</p><p>INDIA bloc parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, have been observing the 12-hour Odisha bandh since 6 am, demanding repeal of the new mining law, the resignation of state minister Nityananda Gond over “errors” in school textbooks and the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.</p><p>“We demand a complete rollback of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar for ‘vote chori’ and state minister Nityananda Gond for distributing books with erroneous information among school students,” senior Congress leader Suresh Routray said in Bhubaneswar.</p><p>Adequate security arrangements have been made across the state to avoid any untoward incidents during the protest, said a senior police officer.</p><p>Efforts have been made to ensure that the protests during the bandh take place democratically and peacefully.</p><p>Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Police Commissioner S Dev Dutta Singh said, “Discussions have been held with various stakeholders so that protesters conduct their demonstrations within the ambit of their constitutional rights.” PTI BBM BBM BDC<div id="1133db14-2b87-4ccf-b1c5-8045d99fd647" data-section="1133db14-2b87-4ccf-b1c5-8045d99fd647" class="_ap_apex_ad" data-xpath="#postcontent > p:eq(8)" data-section-id="" data-ap-network="adpTags" style="display: block; clear: both; text-align: center; margin: 10px auto; width: 728px; height: 90px; overflow: hidden;" data-render-time="1795339835485">

<script data-nopdlab="true">
/*for Font resize*/
$('document').ready(function(){
	var cookie = "fontsize";

	var getFontSize = function(){
		var value = parseInt($.cookie(cookie))
	  return  value||20;
	}

	var changeFontSize = function(direction){
	  var newSize = Math.min(24, Math.max(16, getFontSize()+direction))
	  $.cookie(cookie, newSize, {expires: 30, path: '/', domain  : ''});
	  updateFontSize(newSize)
	}
	var updateFontSize = function(fontsize){
	  var style = $('#font_size_style')
	  if(!style.length){
		style = $('<style id="font_size_style">')
		$(document.body).append(style)
	  }
	  style.text(".td-post-content p { font-size: "+fontsize+"px; line-height: "+(fontsize + 10)+"px;}")
	}

	var initFontSize = function(){
	  var fontsize = getFontSize()
	  console.log(fontsize)
	  updateFontSize(fontsize)
	}

	$(document).ready(initFontSize); 

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#up", function() {        
	  changeFontSize(1)
	});

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#down", function() {
	  changeFontSize(-1)
	}); 
});
</script>

// Dropdown Menu Logic using clean semantic CSS classes
const shareButton = document.getElementById('shareButton');
const shareDropdown = document.getElementById('shareDropdown');
let isDropdownOpen = false;

function toggleDropdown(forceState) {
    isDropdownOpen = forceState !== undefined ? forceState : !isDropdownOpen;
    
    if (isDropdownOpen) {
        shareDropdown.classList.add('is-visible');
        // Small delay to allow display:block to apply before triggering CSS transition
        setTimeout(() => {
            shareDropdown.classList.add('dropdown-enter-active');
        }, 10);
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        shareButton.classList.add('is-active');
    } else {
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('dropdown-enter-active');
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('is-visible');
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        shareButton.classList.remove('is-active');
    }
}

// Toggle on button click
shareButton.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    toggleDropdown();
});

// Close dropdown when clicking outside
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    if (isDropdownOpen && !shareDropdown.contains(e.target) && e.target !== shareButton) {
        toggleDropdown(false);
    }
});

// Prevent closing when clicking inside the dropdown itself
shareDropdown.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
});

// Copy Link to Clipboard function
function copyToClipboard() {
    const url = window.location.href;
    const textArea = document.createElement("textarea");
    textArea.value = url;
    textArea.style.position = "fixed";
    document.body.appendChild(textArea);
    textArea.focus();
    textArea.select();
    try {
        document.execCommand('copy');
        showToast('Link copied to clipboard!');
    } catch (err) {
        console.error('Unable to copy link', err);
    }
    document.body.removeChild(textArea);
    toggleDropdown(false);
}

// Toast notification helper
function showToast(message) {
    const toast = document.createElement('div');
    toast.textContent = message;
    toast.className = 'toast-notification';
    document.body.appendChild(toast);
    
    setTimeout(() => {
        toast.style.opacity = '0';
        setTimeout(() => document.body.removeChild(toast), 300);
    }, 3000);
}</script>	<script type="text/javascript">

Relief for flood victims</h3>The INDIA bloc has also demanded adequate rehabilitation and compensation for people affected by floods in Odisha.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What's likely to remain closed?</h2>The bandh could affect several parts of daily life, although the extent of disruption will vary by location.<br><br><h3>Schools and colleges</h3>Educational institutions may remain closed or suspend normal activities in areas where the bandh has a strong impact. The INDIA bloc has appealed to educational institutions to suspend normal operations during the shutdown. However, students appearing for examinations are not supposed to be stopped from reaching their examination centres. Parents and students should therefore check directly with their schools or colleges before travelling.<br><br><h3>Shops and markets</h3>Markets, shops and commercial establishments are expected to face disruptions, particularly in areas where protesters are holding demonstrations or picketing. The bandh organisers have asked supporters to persuade shops and businesses to remain closed rather than use force.<br><br><h3>Auto-rickshaws</h3>Auto-rickshaw services could be affected in several areas. The Bhubaneswar Auto-rickshaw Mahasangh has indicated that it does not want to risk operating vehicles during the protest because of concerns about possible disruption.<br><br><h3>Public transport</h3>Transport is expected to be among the services most affected. The INDIA bloc has asked buses, auto-rickshaws, trucks and other commercial vehicles to stay off the roads during the bandh. At the same time, the private bus owners' association had said before the bandh that its services would continue unless a fresh decision was taken. This means passengers could see route-specific cancellations, delays or diversions, even where operators have not formally announced a shutdown.<br><br><h2>Are buses running in Odisha today?</h2>The situation is not uniform. Ama Bus services are expected to operate, but routes may be cancelled or diverted depending on the intensity of protests. Private bus operators had also said they intended to operate normally. However, road blockades could still disrupt services in different parts of the state. People travelling by road should therefore allow extra time and check local transport updates before starting their journey.<br><br><h2>What's open during Odisha Bandh?</h2>Essential and emergency services have been kept outside the bandh.<br><br>These include:<br><br><ul><li>Hospitals and nursing homes</li><li>Clinics and emergency medical centres</li><li>Ambulances, including 108 and 102 services</li><li>Blood banks and diagnostic centres</li><li>Pharmacies and Jan Aushadhi Kendras</li><li>Fire and rescue services</li><li>Emergency police services</li><li>Milk distribution and essential milk supplies</li><li>Emergency electricity and water restoration services</li></ul>The bandh organisers have specifically instructed protesters not to obstruct these services.<br><br><h2>Will government offices remain open?</h2>The Odisha government has asked district administrations to ensure the functioning of government offices and essential services. However, government offices could still see disruptions in places where protests, demonstrations or road blockades take place. The state has deployed police personnel and asked officials to maintain law and order.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What about petrol pumps?</h2>Petrol pumps and other commercial establishments could be affected by the bandh in some locations. Reports from Bhubaneswar indicate that several commercial establishments and petrol pumps at prominent locations are expected to remain closed. However, this may not apply uniformly across the state.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What should commuters know?</h2>The biggest impact is expected on road movement. Police have been deployed at sensitive locations, including highways, railway stations and other important points. In Bhubaneswar, around 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force have been deployed to manage the situation, according to the city police. Commuters should avoid unnecessary travel through protest-prone areas and check local traffic updates before leaving home. Emergency vehicles, however, are expected to receive free passage.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"><style>

			  "articleBody":"Odisha Bandh Today: Odisha is observing a 12-hour statewide bandh today, October 8, after opposition parties under the INDIA bloc called for a shutdown over the amended mining law, alleged errors in school textbooks and concerns surrounding the electoral roll revision. The bandh began at 6 am and is scheduled to continue until 6 pm. The protest is expected to affect road transport, markets, educational institutions and some business establishments across the state. The Odisha government has directed district collectors and police officials to take preventive measures and ensure that essential services continue during the shutdown.Odisha Bandh today: Who is protesting?The bandh has been called by the Odisha units of INDIA bloc parties, led by the Congress. The participating parties include the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, according to reports.The alliance has appealed to supporters to hold rallies, demonstrations, picketing and sit-ins while keeping emergency services outside the bandh. The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), however, has decided to stay away from the October 8 bandh. The Naveen Patnaik-led party said it would maintain equal distance from the BJP and Congress.Why is Odisha observing a bandh today?The INDIA bloc has raised several demands behind the shutdown.1. Withdrawal of MMDR Amendment ActThe opposition is demanding the withdrawal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026. The parties have opposed changes to the mining law and raised concerns over the state's rights over its mineral resources.2. Resignation of CEC Gyanesh KumarThe parties are also demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations linked to the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, of electoral rolls. The issue has become a larger political flashpoint, with opposition parties also holding protests in Delhi.3. Resignation of Odisha education ministerThe opposition has sought the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks.4. Relief for flood victimsThe INDIA bloc has also demanded adequate rehabilitation and compensation for people affected by floods in Odisha.Odisha Bandh: What's likely to remain closed?The bandh could affect several parts of daily life, although the extent of disruption will vary by location.Schools and collegesEducational institutions may remain closed or suspend normal activities in areas where the bandh has a strong impact. The INDIA bloc has appealed to educational institutions to suspend normal operations during the shutdown. However, students appearing for examinations are not supposed to be stopped from reaching their examination centres. Parents and students should therefore check directly with their schools or colleges before travelling.Shops and marketsMarkets, shops and commercial establishments are expected to face disruptions, particularly in areas where protesters are holding demonstrations or picketing. The bandh organisers have asked supporters to persuade shops and businesses to remain closed rather than use force.Auto-rickshawsAuto-rickshaw services could be affected in several areas. The Bhubaneswar Auto-rickshaw Mahasangh has indicated that it does not want to risk operating vehicles during the protest because of concerns about possible disruption.Public transportTransport is expected to be among the services most affected. The INDIA bloc has asked buses, auto-rickshaws, trucks and other commercial vehicles to stay off the roads during the bandh. At the same time, the private bus owners' association had said before the bandh that its services would continue unless a fresh decision was taken. This means passengers could see route-specific cancellations, delays or diversions, even where operators have not formally announced a shutdown.Are buses running in Odisha today?The situation is not uniform. Ama Bus services are expected to operate, but routes may be cancelled or diverted depending on the intensity of protests. Private bus operators had also said they intended to operate normally. However, road blockades could still disrupt services in different parts of the state. People travelling by road should therefore allow extra time and check local transport updates before starting their journey.What's open during Odisha Bandh?Essential and emergency services have been kept outside the bandh.These include:Hospitals and nursing homesClinics and emergency medical centresAmbulances, including 108 and 102 servicesBlood banks and diagnostic centresPharmacies and Jan Aushadhi KendrasFire and rescue servicesEmergency police servicesMilk distribution and essential milk suppliesEmergency electricity and water restoration servicesThe bandh organisers have specifically instructed protesters not to obstruct these services.Will government offices remain open?The Odisha government has asked district administrations to ensure the functioning of government offices and essential services. However, government offices could still see disruptions in places where protests, demonstrations or road blockades take place. The state has deployed police personnel and asked officials to maintain law and order.Odisha Bandh: What about petrol pumps?Petrol pumps and other commercial establishments could be affected by the bandh in some locations. Reports from Bhubaneswar indicate that several commercial establishments and petrol pumps at prominent locations are expected to remain closed. However, this may not apply uniformly across the state.Odisha Bandh: What should commuters know?The biggest impact is expected on road movement. Police have been deployed at sensitive locations, including highways, railway stations and other important points. In Bhubaneswar, around 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force have been deployed to manage the situation, according to the city police. Commuters should avoid unnecessary travel through protest-prone areas and check local traffic updates before leaving home. Emergency vehicles, however, are expected to receive free passage.",

    "articleBody" : "Bhubaneswar: The Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (OPCC) president Bhakta Charan Das on Tuesday announced a statewide strike ‘Odisha Bandh’ by the political parties of the India Bloc on October 8 over various demands, including the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, the resignation of state School and Mass Education (S&ME) minister Nityananda Gond and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Speaking to media persons, the OPCC president said, “The political parties of the INDIA bloc are protesting over three demands, including the repeal of the MMDR Amendment Act, the resignation and arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, and Odisha’s education minister Nityananda Gond’s resignation.”He further said that the INDIA bloc had planned to gherao the Odisha Assembly on Tuesday. Das alleged that the state government, fearing the protest, adjourned the session sine die, even though it was scheduled to continue until October 3.“So, the agitation will intensify further, and Odisha, from the capital Bhubaneswar to every village, will remain shut down on October 8. Thousands of workers of all the INDIA bloc political parties will court arrest,” said the OPCC president.Meanwhile, the political parties of the INDIA bloc, led by the Odisha Congress, on Tuesday held a massive protest rally, 'Parivartan Rally' in Bhubaneswar against the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, the resignation of state School and Mass Education (S&ME) minister Nityanand Gond over the school textbook error issue and the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) over alleged electoral process irregularities.The members and leaders of Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP-Sharad Pawar, Samajwadi Party and RJD from across the state participated in the Parivartan Rally.After a huge protest meeting at the Lower PMG, the protestors marched towards the Chief Minister’s residence to stage a gherao to register their protest. Senior leaders from Congress and other political parties addressed the workers at the protest meeting.Tension prevailed at Lower PMG as protesters clashed with police after they were stopped from marching ahead. To bring the situation under control, security personnel later detained several senior leaders and workers of the India bloc and took them away from the protest site.It is worth mentioning here that the opposition Biju Janata Dal also organised a massive protest rally in Bhubaneswar demanding the repeal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026 on Monday. Senior leaders from Congress and other political parties addressed the workers at the protest meeting.</p><p>Tension prevailed at Lower PMG as protesters clashed with police after they were stopped from marching ahead. To bring the situation under control, security personnel later detained several senior leaders and workers of the India bloc and took them away from the protest site.</p><p>It is worth mentioning here <script>
(function () {


const SITES = [
    { name: "Dinamani", url: "https://www.dinamani.com" },
    { name: "Kannada Prabha", url: "https://www.kannadaprabha.com" },
    { name: "Samakalika Malayalam", url: "https://www.samakalikamalayalam.com" },
    { name: "Cinema Express", url: "https://www.cinemaexpress.com" },
    { name: "Indulgexpress", url: "https://www.indulgexpress.com" },
    { name: "Edexlive", url: "https://www.edexlive.com" }
];


function init() {


    if (document.getElementById("network-strip")) return;
    const navbar = document.querySelector("#navbar");
    if (!navbar) return;
    const style = document.createElement("style");
    style.innerHTML = `
#network-strip{
    width:100%;
    background:#fff;
    border-bottom:1px solid #e5e5e5;
    overflow:hidden;
    font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif;
    box-sizing:border-box;
}


#network-strip .network-scroll{
    overflow-x:auto;
    overflow-y:hidden;
    -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch;
    scrollbar-width:none;
    touch-action:pan-x;
    scroll-behavior:smooth;
}


#network-strip .network-scroll::-webkit-scrollbar{
    display:none;
}


#network-strip .network-list{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    justify-content:center;
    list-style:none;
    margin:0;
    padding:8px 20px;
    white-space:nowrap;
    width:max-content;
    min-width:100%;
}


#network-strip .network-list li{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    flex:0 0 auto;
}


#network-strip .network-list li:not(:last-child)::after{
    content:"|";
    color:#bdbdbd;
    margin:0 14px;
}


#network-strip .network-list a{
    color:#555;
    text-decoration:none;
    font-size:15px;
    font-weight:500;
    transition:.2s;
}


#network-strip .network-list a:hover{
    color:#000;
}


@media(max-width:768px){


    #network-strip .network-list{
        justify-content:flex-start;
        min-width:max-content;
        padding:8px 16px;
    }


    #network-strip .network-list a{
        font-size:12px;
    }


    #network-strip .network-list li:not(:last-child)::after{
        margin:0 10px;
    }


}
`;


    document.head.appendChild(style);


    const strip = document.createElement("div");
    strip.id = "network-strip";


    const scroll = document.createElement("div");
    scroll.className = "network-scroll";


    const ul = document.createElement("ul");
    ul.className = "network-list";


    SITES.forEach(site => {


        const li = document.createElement("li");


        const a = document.createElement("a");
        a.href = site.url;
        a.target = "_blank";
        a.rel = "noopener noreferrer";
        a.textContent = site.name;


        li.appendChild(a);
        ul.appendChild(li);


    });


    scroll.appendChild(ul);
    strip.appendChild(scroll);


    navbar.prepend(strip);


}


if (document.readyState === "loading") {
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);
} else {
    init();
}


})();

one passing through Satara, Rahimatpur, Vita, Tasgaon, Miraj, Gokak and Belagavi, and the second through Satara, Karad, Islampur, Ashta, Miraj, Kagwad, Gokak and Belagavi.</p><p>The police have requested Google Maps to display alerts about the road closure, inform commuters about traffic congestion and delays, and refrain from directing vehicles through the affected stretch until the agitation ends. The platform has also been asked to suggest alternative routes, he said.</p><p>The request has been made in view of the safety of long-distance passenger vehicles and heavy goods vehicles travelling along the highway, he said.</p><p>The police will inform Google Maps once traffic movement returns to normal so that the closure-related advisories can be withdrawn, the officer said.</p><p>Necessary arrangements have been made along these alternative routes with the help of traffic police and local police personnel, Sharma said, urging people to use them if their travel is unavoidable.</p><p><em>(With inputs from PTI)</em></p></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div data-test-id="promotional-message" class="arrow-component arr--text-element text-m_promotionalMessage__CUsPM text-m_dark__1TC18 "><div><p><strong><ins><a aria-label="content" target="_self" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaAJz0Q2f3EFfUEev01O">Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp</a> </ins></strong></p><p><strong><a aria-label="content" target="_self" href="https://onelink.to/heh8j3">Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest</a></strong></p><p></p></div></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div id="widget-inreads_1x1-663ea6b7-17ef-46aa-b901-e3f15302723c" data-test-id="widget" class="app-ad app-ad--story-horizontal widget-m__widget__bUJP1" style="--widget-height-mobile: 220px; traffic on the busy Mumbai-Bengaluru National Highway was disrupted on Wednesday due to a farmers' protest on the Maharashtra-Karnataka border, prompting police to advise commuters to avoid the route and request Google Maps to mark the affected stretch as closed.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInspector General of Police, Kolhapur Range, Ranjan Kumar Sharma advised people to use alternative routes.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe police have also written to Google Maps authorities, requesting to mark the affected stretch of National Highway no. 48 as closed due to the agitation underway at the Kognoli toll plaza in Karnataka along the Maharashtra border.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFarmers have been staging the protest over sugarcane prices, ethanol rates and other demands since Tuesday morning.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe agitation has affected traffic moving from Kolhapur and other parts of Maharashtra towards Belagavi and Bengaluru in Karnataka.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe situation remained unchanged on Wednesday morning, as per the office of Pune Range Superintendent of Police (Highway) Dr Shivaji Pawar.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe police urged commuters to avoid travelling on NH-48 unless necessary, as the agitation led to traffic congestion and the situation may take time to normalise.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESharma said commuters would be informed once the situation improves.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe police have identified two alternative routes for the convenience of travellers - one passing through Satara, Rahimatpur, Vita, Tasgaon, Miraj, Gokak and Belagavi, and the second through Satara, Karad, Islampur, Ashta, Miraj, Kagwad, Gokak and Belagavi.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe police have requested Google Maps to display alerts about the road closure, inform commuters about traffic congestion and delays, and refrain from directing vehicles through the affected stretch until the agitation ends. The platform has also been asked to suggest alternative routes, he said.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe request has been made in view of the safety of long-distance passenger vehicles and heavy goods vehicles travelling along the highway, he said.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe police will inform Google Maps once traffic movement returns to normal so that the closure-related advisories The delay in completing the 34.5-km six-laning of Sriperumbudur-Karaipettai section of Chennai-Bengaluru highway, launched eight years ago, continues to cause severe hardship to commuters. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has missed several deadlines for the project and has so far only completed eight of the 17 planned flyovers, bridges and vehicular underpasses along the stretch. NHAI has now set August 2027 as the revised deadline for completing the project.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe existing 15 m wide carriageway narrows to 7.5 m, with traffic diverted to service lanes on either side for nearly 3.5 km to facilitate the construction of vehicular underpasses at Mambakkam and near Sipcot in Sriperumbudur. As a result, vehicles take nearly 60 to 90 minutes to cover the 10 km stretch between Sriperumbudur and Sunguvarchathiram.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECommuters said the prolonged construction work had been causing severe hardship despite the highway being tolled. The situation worsens during weekends and festival seasons when the traffic volume increases. During the recent Deepavali festival, vehicles were stranded in queues stretching up to 9 km between Sunguvarchathiram and Sriperumbudur from November 5 to 10, with congestion persisting throughout the day.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOfficials from the NHAI’s Kancheepuram project unit said vehicular underpasses and flyovers at Sunguvarchathiram East and West, Santhavellore, Senthamangalam, through Thampanoor during the evening rush has become a nightmare for commuters, particularly along the Model School-Aristo Junction stretch. \u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECongestion begins around 5pm on working days and often continues late into the night, affecting traffic from Panavila to Thampanoor.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrivate long-distance buses parked along the roadside occupy almost an entire lane. KSRTC buses and other motorists must squeeze through what remains, and traffic slows to a crawl.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe problem began when private operators shifted their boarding point from Sangeetha College Road after it was closed for Smart Road construction. Even after the work was completed, they kept using the present stretch. Buses are often brought out of their parking yards well before departure and left at the roadside.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cstrong\u003EAn everyday ordeal\u003C\u002Fstrong\u003E\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“Travelling through this stretch during the evening hours is extremely difficult,” says Rajesh Kumar, a private-sector employee. \u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“Even if you have to cover a short distance, you end up spending a long time in traffic. The private buses are parked one after another. This has been going on for a long time, and it is high time the authorities found a permanent solution.”\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnjana S, a bank employee, points to added pressure from the railway station. “Whenever a major train arrives, the roads get crowded with vehicles coming to pick up and drop off passengers,” she says. \u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“With these private buses occupying an entire lane, the situation becomes even worse. When it rains, waterlogging makes it harder.”\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAshok K, a tourism professional, says seven compounds in and around the stretch offer daily-rent parking for private buses, yet some operators still use the roadside. \u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“Operators say they will leave once the passengers board. However, when passengers arrive late, the buses remain there. Families also bring their vehicles to drop them off,” he says.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEven ambulances, he adds, often get caught in the snarls. “The police intervene and warn the operators, and the situation improves for a few days. But soon, things return to the way they were. This has been a recurring problem,” he plan back in focus\u003C\u002Fstrong\u003E\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA long-pending proposal to shift long-distance bus operations to Enchakkal is back on the government’s agenda.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETransport Minister C P John recently announced that the state was fast-tracking the development of KSRTC land there into an integrated long-distance and interstate bus hub.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFirst mooted in 2004, the project is reportedly planned on 5.79 acres of KSRTC land alongside NH 66, close to the international airport.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPreliminary work has begun. “The hub will house KSRTC long-distance, private long-distance and interstate services, with dedicated parking and operational facilities,” says an official.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnilkumar Pandala, former managing director of the Thiruvananthapuram Road Development Authority, says Enchakkal was part of a broader plan under the Thiruvananthapuram City Improvement Project.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“The first step was to shift the services from East Fort to Thampanoor, followed by moving inter-district services from Thampanoor to Enchakkal,” he says. “Since five acres are already available, it would be better to start interstate services from there.”\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERelocation talks have raised concerns among those who depend on the passengers the buses bring. At least 18 travel agencies operate in Thampanoor, along with shops, lodges and taxi\u002Fauto-rickshaw services.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThampanoor currently hosts buses to Wayanad, Kannur, Hyderabad, Chennai, Bengaluru, Velankanni, Mookambika, Puducherry, Manipal, Mangaluru and Coimbatore.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAuto driver Ajayan B says the arrival of trains, particularly the Vande Bharat Express, brings traffic to a standstill for nearly an hour. Private buses caused problems earlier, he says, but the situation has improved. “These buses bring us passengers,” he says.  \u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBaiju Poovathur, who has run a shop near the stretch for two decades, echoes the sentiment. “Our livelihoods are linked to these buses,” he says.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPraveen Kumar V R, treasurer of the Travel Agencies’ Association, says the administration should first improve basic facilities. “Sangeetha College Road has been a boarding point for years, but there is no proper shelter for passengers, or adequate amenities such as toilets and cloakroom,” he says.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“We believe a properly equipped space within the city limits would be better than moving everything to
